request-transform-coil.title: Network cache policy remains enabled
request-transform-coil.description: This disables only the disk cache. The network cache policy keeps its default of ENABLED, so Coil does not add the `no-cache, no-store` request header described in the fixture. The assertion in the MockEngine therefore fails because the expected `no-store` value is absent.
request-transform-coil.evidence: The changed line sets `.diskCachePolicy(CachePolicy.DISABLED)` but does not configure the network cache policy; the fixture states its default is ENABLED and that the expected header requires disabled disk reads/writes plus enabled network reads.
request-transform-coil.suggestion: Also disable the network cache policy so Coil emits the expected request header.

request-transform-write.title: Private image requests can reach transport without no-store
request-transform-write.description: The changed policy enables disk writes while disabling disk reads. In that configuration, `newRequest` sets `Cache-Control` to `no-cache`, which does not include `no-store`. The middleware and application request preserve those headers, and the transport receives the same value; the test therefore throws because its required directive is absent.
request-transform-write.evidence: The exact policy is `{ diskRead: false, diskWrite: true, networkRead: true }`. The condition passes, the ternary selects `"no-cache"`, and `transport(request)` returns that header unchanged. `testTransport` checks for `no-store` and fails.
request-transform-write.suggestion: Ensure the private-request policy includes `no-store` in the Cache-Control header sent to transport, including when disk writes are enabled.

request-transform-bypass.title: Application request bypasses the no-store header builder
request-transform-bypass.description: `applicationRequest` constructs and returns a fresh request instead of using the header-producing request builder. The outgoing request therefore has no `Cache-Control` header, so `testTransport` throws because the transport does not observe `no-store`.
request-transform-bypass.evidence: The changed line initializes `request.headers` as `{}`; the downstream assertion checks `transport(request)` for `no-store` and fails when the header is absent.
request-transform-bypass.suggestion: Build the application request through the header-producing builder while preserving any required upstream headers.

request-transform-overwrite.title: Downstream assignment removes the required no-store directive
request-transform-overwrite.description: The unchanged request builder sets `Cache-Control` to `no-cache, no-store` because `networkRead` is true and `diskRead` is false. `applicationRequest` then replaces that value with `no-cache` before the request reaches `transport`, so the transport receives a header without `no-store` and `testTransport` throws.
request-transform-overwrite.evidence: `request.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-cache"` replaces the builder's `"no-cache, no-store"` value; `transport` returns the replaced header and the test rejects it when it lacks `no-store`.
request-transform-overwrite.suggestion: Preserve the policy-derived header value instead of overwriting it.

request-transform-mock.title: Production request omits the required no-store header
request-transform-mock.description: `applicationRequest()` constructs a request with empty headers, and the production path passes it to `transport()` without `testTransport()`. Consequently, the outgoing request has no `Cache-Control: no-store` directive. The shown test does not verify production behavior because its mock mutates the request before asserting.
request-transform-mock.evidence: The changed construction is `const request = { headers: {} };`; `transport()` reads `request.headers["Cache-Control"]`, while only `testTransport()` adds that header.
request-transform-mock.suggestion: Set the required `Cache-Control` header when constructing the production request.

request-transform-utf8.title: Byte truncation can produce invalid UTF-8
request-transform-utf8.description: The encoded text for `é` is the two-byte UTF-8 sequence `C3 A9`. Slicing to one byte retains only `C3`, so the strict decoder throws instead of producing a valid preview. Truncation must avoid splitting a multibyte character.
request-transform-utf8.evidence: `new TextEncoder().encode("é")` yields two UTF-8 bytes, and `slice(0, 1)` passes only the leading byte to `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })`, which rejects it as malformed input.
request-transform-utf8.suggestion: Truncate at a UTF-8 code point boundary, or decode non-fatally if replacement characters are acceptable under the preview contract.

request-transform-bypass.title: Application request bypasses the no-store header builder
request-transform-bypass.description: `applicationRequest` creates a fresh request instead of using `middleware()`, which calls `newRequest()` and supplies `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-store`. The outgoing request therefore has no `Cache-Control` header, and `testTransport` throws because the transport observation does not include `no-store`.

request-transform-overwrite.title: Downstream assignment removes the required no-store directive
request-transform-overwrite.description: The upstream builder sets `Cache-Control` to `no-cache, no-store` for the shown policy, but `applicationRequest` overwrites it with `no-cache` before the transport observes the request. The transport assertion therefore fails because the outgoing header lacks `no-store`.
request-transform-overwrite.evidence: `newRequest` assigns `no-cache, no-store` when `networkRead` is true and `diskRead` is false; the changed assignment replaces that value, and `testTransport` requires the transport-observed header to include `no-store`.
request-transform-overwrite.suggestion: Preserve the upstream policy-derived header instead of replacing it with `no-cache`.

request-transform-mock.title: Production request omits the no-store header
request-transform-mock.description: `applicationRequest` constructs a request with empty headers and returns it without applying `middleware` or adding the cache policy. The described production path passes this request to `transport`, so it can send without the required `no-store` directive. The test mock does not demonstrate production behavior because it adds the directive before calling `transport`.
request-transform-mock.evidence: The changed construction is `const request = { headers: {} };`; `transport` reads `request.headers["Cache-Control"]`, while the shown `testTransport` mutates that header before asserting.
request-transform-mock.suggestion: Apply the no-store policy when constructing the production request before it reaches `transport`.

request-transform-utf8.title: Byte truncation produces invalid UTF-8
request-transform-utf8.description: The encoded string `é` is two UTF-8 bytes (`C3 A9`), but slicing to one byte leaves the incomplete sequence `C3`. The following strict UTF-8 decoder rejects it, violating the preview contract and throwing instead of producing a valid preview.
request-transform-utf8.evidence: `new TextEncoder().encode("é")` produces two bytes; `.slice(0, 1)` retains only the first, and `TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true })` rejects that incomplete sequence.
request-transform-utf8.suggestion: Truncate at a valid UTF-8 code point boundary, or decode non-fatally if replacement characters are acceptable for the preview contract.
